$comment: Hostile third-party rich text, for W14's sanitisation tests.
Synthetic and entirely invented, like everything in fixtures/. It is written to
look like what a document tool actually hands back after somebody pastes from the
open web: markup, a javascript: link, a data: URI, control characters, and
bidirectional overrides that make a title render as something other than what it
is. docs/14-threat-model.md §2 boundary 5 — this content flows into rendering
AND into an agent's context, which is why 'it's the owner's own workspace' is not
Every entry is deliberately something a sanitiser could get wrong, not something
obviously bad. A test fixture of <script>alert(1)</script> and nothing else
proves only that the easy case is handled.

runs.$note: U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE and U+202C POP. Renders as 'Invoice exe.txt' in a UI and reads as something it is not.

CR, NUL, BEL and ESC, escaped because raw control characters are not legal JSON. They arrive from a tool's API, not from a file anybody types — and the CR is the one that silently changes a content hash.
